articles.title: Yankees let pitcher Luis Gil go, declining to tender contract 2 seasons after winning AL Rookie of the Year
articles.summary: Gil had been injured throughout the past two seasons and struggled with walks while pitching in relief.
articles.body:
Two years after Luis Gil won American League Rookie of the Year honors , the New York Yankees decided not to tender a contract to the right-hander, making him a free agent.

The decision came before Friday's 5 p.m. ET deadline for offering contracts to players still under club control.

Gil compiled a 3.50 ERA, a 15-7 record and 171 strikeouts in 151 1/3 innings during the 2024 season, looking like a part of the Yankees' starting rotation for years to come.

However, he suffered a high-grade right lat strain during spring training the following season. That sidelined Gil until August. He was effective upon his return, compiling a 3.32 ERA in 11 starts, but his strikeout rate dropped from 10.1 batters per nine innings to 6.5.

This past season, Gil struggled during spring training and was not part of the Yankees' opening day starting rotation .

He joined the major-league roster in April, but registered a 6.05 ERA in four starts (allowing 13 runs in 19 1/3 innings) and was demoted back to Triple-A. While with Scranton/Wilkes-Barre, Gil was placed on the injured list with shoulder inflammation and shut down for three months.

Called up just before September, Gil worked out of the bullpen and compiled a 4.61 ERA in five appearances. However, control was a major issue — as it was throughout his Yankees career — with seven walks in eight innings. Ultimately, he was assigned to the Yankees' Florida rookie league affiliate in late September and left off their postseason roster.

Gil, 28, was set for his first year of arbitration eligibility next spring.

The Yankees also non-tendered reliever Fernando Cruz. The 36-year-old right-hander made 61 appearances, striking out 67 batters in 54 2/3 innings. But he sustained a partially torn ulnar collateral ligament in late August, ending his season.

Cruz was acquired before the 2025 season from the Cincinnati Reds in a trade for catcher Jose Trevino. He was one of the Yankees' most effective relievers, notching 72 strikeouts in 48 innings.

articles.title: Giants make major change in stance on Logan Webb trade rumors
articles.summary: This is a surprising update for the Giants on the potential of a Logan Webb trade.
articles.body:
The San Francisco Giants sold off a few key players at the MLB trade deadline this past season, but they didn't move any core players signed to long-term deals.

That could change this offseason, with Rafael Devers, Matt Chapman, and Willy Adames as names to watch who could be on the move. However, a new name has emerged as one this Giants team is willing to listen to offers for: Logan Webb.

According to MLB insider Robert Murray of Fansided.com , the Giants have taken a major change in stance on the Webb trade rumors, as they're now open to offers for the star right-hander this offseason.

Giants open to trade offers for Logan Webb

"For years, the San Francisco Giants refused to engage or listen to any inquiries involving star right-handed pitcher Logan Webb. That is no longer the case," Murray reports. "The Giants are open to listening to offers for Webb, multiple rival executives say."

This is a huge change in stance from the Giants, as they've been steadfast in recent years that Webb isn't going anywhere. They shut down trade offers for him at this past MLB trade deadline.

The 30-year-old right-hander would fetch a huge return if traded, and now it appears the Giants are open to a trade, as they're listening to offers for Webb.

He might not actually be traded this offseason, or ever, by the Giants. But their willingness to listen to trade inquiries is still a major shift in philosophy for the Giants.

Webb is signed for the next two seasons on his five-year, $90 million deal. There are bound to be plenty of teams willing to make a push to acquire Webb.

Teams that miss out on Tarik Skubal and some of the other top free agent starters might turn to the Giants for a Webb trade.

Before, the Giants would turn down all offers. Now, they're open to a deal, as they're reportedly going to listen to trade offers for Webb going forward.

This is a huge update for the Giants from an MLB insider, and should have their fanbase on high alert. This team trading away players makes sense, but Webb has been off-limits. That is no longer the case, as he's now seemingly available for trade.

articles.title: New MLB Trade Rumors on Logan Webb's Availability, Giants' Stance amid Free Agency
articles.summary: The San Francisco Giants are willing to field offers for star pitcher Logan Webb on the trade market, according to Robert Murray of FanSided.
articles.body:
The San Francisco Giants are willing to field offers for star pitcher Logan Webb on the trade market, according to Robert Murray of FanSided.

"For years, the San Francisco Giants have refused to engage or listen to any inquiries involving star right-handed pitcher Logan Webb. That is no longer the case," Murray reported Saturday. "The Giants are open to listening to offers for Webb, multiple rival executives say."

According to The Athletic's Ken Rosenthal and Will Sammon , "San Francisco would want a 'very strong return' for Webb, according to a person briefed on the team's plans who was not authorized to discuss trade conversations publicly. And while a number of clubs are desperate to add starting pitching, some rival executives are skeptical the Giants will get their price."

Webb has spent all eight years of his MLB career in San Francisco and has earned All-Star honors in each of the past three seasons.

The Giants are coming off a 2026 campaign in which they finished with a 65-97 record.

They sold during last season's trade deadline, parting ways with important contributors including Luis Arráez, Robbie Ray, Tyler Mahle and Heliot Ramos.

Webb wasn't available at the time. Ken Rosenthal of The Athletic reported that San Francisco had "zero plans" to trade the right-hander in June.

That doesn't seem to be the case anymore.

Webb has two seasons remaining on a five-year, $90 million extension that he signed with the Giants in 2023. He'll earn $23 million during the 2027 season before he's set to receive $24 million in 2028 (via Spotrac ).

He made 27 starts during the 2026 season, compiling an 8-9 record to go along with a 4.31 ERA and 1.170 WHIP. Webb amassed 134 strikeouts compared to 41 walks in 160.2 innings of work.

The 30-year-old has been a consistent part of San Francisco's rotation throughout his career, posting a 3.19 ERA across 159 total games from 2021-25.

articles.title: Yankees Receive Spencer Jones Take From Insider Amid Trade Interest
articles.summary: The New York Yankees are garnering trade interest for outfielder Spencer Jones. Recently, Yankees general manager Brian Cashman confirmed that teams are call...
articles.body:
The New York Yankees are garnering trade interest for outfielder Spencer Jones. Recently, Yankees general manager Brian Cashman confirmed that teams are calling about Jones. "He's someone that teams are asking a lot about," Cashman said in a Nov. 19 article from The Athletic's Brendan Kuty. "I'm not here to say if he's our center fielder or not. I just think we're going to remain opportunistic in the marketplace and see what's available."Now, the question is: Should the Yankees have him on the table as part of any blockbuster trade to improve the team for next season? For MLB insider Jim Duquette, New York absolutely should consider using Jones as a trade chip to address any major weakness on the team. "I think Jones absolutely should be on the table," Duquette said in a Nov. 20 video from "Baseball Night in New Jersey." "[The Yankees] don't. That's the thing. We see this a lot with them. They hold on to their guys, and then all of a sudden, they hold on to them a little longer, and all of a sudden, there's no value there with [Anthony] Volpe. I think the same thing might happen with [Austin] Wells. If he doesn't bounce back, eventually you're going to wonder why they didn't move him when they should have. "Jones is in that boat for me just because of the strikeouts. In fairness, he has made some adjustments, and he's looked better than the reports coming out of the minor leagues, where he had a strikeout rate over 30 percent. I do think they should consider that, but it didn't seem like they were willing to move any of their young players."

Should Yankees Take Risk of Trading Spencer Jones?

Moreover, in the same segment, John Jastremski also believes that the Yankees should consider using Jones as a trade chip, even though the risk is that the outfielder could turn into a stud major leaguer. "Listen, Spencer Jones may turn out to be a guy that goes 30-30 in the big leagues," Jastremski added. "He may end up having a really good career [and] he's a good glove. He hits left-handed pitching [and] played well last year [and] is another one of these guys that's left-handed and strikes out a zillion times. The Yankees need a different look to their lineup."

Last season for the Yankees, Jones hit .245 with 64 hits, 11 home runs, 40 RBIs, and 36 runs scored in 86 games, per StatMuse.

New York Gets Free Agency Take on Randy Arozarena

Meanwhile, when it comes to free agents, Xavier Scruggs of MLB Network Radio on SiriusXM issued an intriguing message regarding Seattle Mariners free agent Randy Arozarena. Scruggs believes that Arozarena has what it takes to put on the pinstripes and play in New York. "They've got to get creative and find a way to bring in a right-handed hitter with some thump," Scruggs said in a Nov. 18 video from MLB Network Radio on SiriusXM. "There's no doubt about that. The Yankees' right-handed hitters had a .709 OPS. Randy Arozarena would easily fix that, and that is the focus for them."If we've got to be creative to bring in someone like Randy Arozarena, I think they should do that because, again, we've talked about how the left-on-left matchups can hurt them at times. If they want to combat that, they bring in someone like Randy. Also, you mentioned earlier that his pedigree of being on the big stage previously plays into his ability to play in New York, with him having a ridiculous postseason pedigree so far in his career."Last season for the Mariners, Arozarena had a batting average of .281 with 161 hits, 26 home runs, 79 RBIs, and 113 runs scored in 154 games, per StatMuse.

articles.title: 2026 MLB Free Agents Rumors, Predictions for Yankees, Dodgers and Mets
articles.summary: The free agency period in MLB is underway, with front offices around the game attempting to acquire the players they believe will help them get into playoff contention and to compete for a World Series.
articles.body:
The free agency period in MLB is underway, with front offices around the game attempting to acquire the players they believe will help them get into playoff contention and to compete for a World Series.

Starting pitcher Tarik Skubal is the top prize in free agency, but veteran hitters like Randy Arozarena and Ty France also figure to have numerous suitors.

Dive deeper into the latest surrounding each star in this collection of insider reports.

The Bronx Bombers reportedly have their eye on one of the top hitters in this year's free agency class.

Jon Heyman of the New York Post (h/t MLB.com ) reported that the Yankees are interested in adding a right-handed hitter to a predominantly left-handed lineup.

Arozarena was the best part of a struggling Mariners offense in 2026, hitting .281/.381/.484 with a .865 OPS, 26 home runs, 79 RBIs, 113 hits, and 26 stolen bases.

It is no wonder that a team that shrank offensively in the playoffs, as the Yankees did, would be interested in adding the 31-year-old's bat to the lineup.

Especially after owner Hal Steinbrenner specifically laid blame for the team's shortcomings at the feet of the offensive skill players.

The Orioles and Phillies, two teams also in need of offensive help, are also looking at adding Arozarena to their lineups.

The former of the two typically does not spend in free agency. The Phillies, though, would be a great fit for the veteran outfielder. That there is a sense of desperation within that organization to win now may be the difference between him joining Philadelphia and any other potential suitor.

Prediction: Arozarena signs with Philadelphia

Dodgers Face Stiff Competition for Skubal

The Los Angeles Dodgers may be the incumbent team when it comes to starting pitcher Tarik Skubal, and the two-time Cy Young winner may have enjoyed his time with the organization, but that does not mean the team has the upper hand in free agency.

Former MLB general manager and MLB Network Radio analyst John Duquette reported that the New York Mets' first offer to Skubal was for nine years, $400 million, the highest AAV for a starting pitcher in baseball history.

That is an otherworldly number for a 30-year-old pitcher coming off of arm surgery , but it is indicative of the respect Skubal has earned around the league as the top ace in the game.

Even in a "down" season compared to his two Cy Young campaigns, Skubal was brilliant, going 12-7 in 26 appearances, with a 2.72 ERA, 186 strikeouts, and a 0.964 WHIP.

A fantastic starter who can go deep into any game, he is a franchise-changing starter for many teams contending for a World Series, hence the Mets' reported willingness to throw a big, possibly insurmountable offer out there early.

The Toronto Blue Jays are reportedly in on Skubal, too, meaning the competition for the Dodgers will be plentiful. Whether the Mets and Blue Jays' offers will be used to bid Los Angeles up, or if the Dodgers really will lose out on the lefty, is the question.

Mets Interested in Free Agent Outfielder

Heyman reported for the New York Post that the Mets are interested in acquiring Ty France this offseason.

The 32-year-old hit .295, with 21 home runs, 78 RBIs, and 24 stolen bases. He is a former Gold Glove winner at first base, a position of great need for the Mets, which became readily apparent in the wake of Pete Alonso signing with the Orioles last season.

France is looking to capitalize on his best season in years, with multiple teams looking to acquire his services, including the incumbent San Diego Padres.

If the Mets are serious about spending in an attempt to get back into World Series contention, France makes sense at a position of need. If the organization is looking to give Tarik Skubal $400 million, though, the front office's willingness to spend in other areas would seemingly take a hit.

articles.title: How Francisco Lindor balances fatherhood, family responsibilities and the pressure of being a New York Mets MLB superstar while raising three children with wife Katia Reguero
articles.summary: Discover how New York Mets superstar Francisco Lindor navigates the challenges of being an MLB athlete while prioritizing his family life and community contributions.
articles.body: Francisco Lindor is one of the most recognizable shortstops in Major League Baseball, and his play for the New York Mets has made him a big part of the lineup. But away from the rigors of professional baseball, the Puerto Rican star has another equally important role: being a present husband and father. Since becoming a parent, his approach to juggling both worlds has changed quite a bit.Francisco is married to Katia Reguero Lindor. They have three children, daughters Kalina Zoe and Amapola Chloe, and son Koa Amani, born in March 2025. Lindor has stressed the importance of keeping family first throughout his life, even with the demanding travel schedule, training, and expectations of being an MLB superstar. His story is a case study in how personal priorities can change, even for athletes who are competing at the very highest level.How Francisco Lindor separates baseball from family responsibilitiesFor Lindor, it’s a deliberate change in mindset as he moves from life as a professional baseball player to life as a family man. Being a New York Met means you’re constantly under the microscope, under pressure to perform, to produce consistent results. But he’s learned those responsibilities don’t have to dictate every part of his personal life.Baseball used to be about 85% of his life, Lindor told Haute Living, explaining that his family responsibilities changed his priorities. He started to re-think how much time he spent on the sport outside of work, once he became a husband and father. Eventually, he learned to back off and give his wife and children more space, rather than letting baseball control his daily schedule.He also reviews his games before he goes home. This allows him time to digest his thoughts on the performance before focusing on recovery and his family life. His family life thus provides an alternative space to the competitive environment of Major League Baseball. For Lindor, that means trying to create a healthier dividing line between his professional accomplishments and his personal relationships instead of letting individual performances dictate his mood for the rest of the day.How Francisco Lindor prioritizes family during MLB seasonThe MLB schedule makes it difficult for players to keep up with a consistent family routine. 162 regular season games, regular road trips, training and recovery commitments all mean that quality time at home can be a challenge.Lindor has attempted to overcome this hurdle by moving a lot of his physical preparation to his home. He said he invested in an at-home gym, recovery equipment, and a daily massage therapist who comes to his residence, in his interview with Haute Living. The arrangements allow him to meet important fitness and recovery activities without regularly spending extra hours away from his family.That’s especially important during the regular season, when being fit is a big part of staying in the Mets’ lineup. Recovery becomes easier, and Lindor can balance his professional duties with more time for his children.His dedication to family responsibilities also surfaced following the arrival of his youngest child. Katia welcomed their son Koa in Orlando on March 30, 2025. Lindor then joined the Mets in Miami the next day and was available for the team’s series opener against the Miami Marlins.Lindor told manager Carlos Mendoza of his plans and got to the ballpark before the game, MLB.com reported. And even if he didn’t get started that night, his choice was emblematic of the push and pull between his family responsibilities and work duties at a pivotal moment in his life.He also credited Katia for helping to keep the home front stable while he traveled for baseball. Lindor described their relationship as a partnership, supporting each other while raising their kids and passing on important family values.Katia Reguero Lindor supports family and careerKatia Reguero Lindor is busy keeping the family routine going while also pursuing her own interests. She's more than a ballplayer's wife. She is a professional violinist and has her own platform with her podcast, The Un-a-Parent, about parenting issues.In a 2026 interview with People, Katia said she started the bilingual podcast in 2022 after becoming a mom and wanting to create a space for parents to talk about their struggles. It has since evolved into a platform covering parenting, mental health, and other social subjects.Fatherhood has also influenced how Lindor deals with the expectations and criticism that come with playing in a major American sports market. He was under a microscope when he came to the Mets in a deal from Cleveland in 2021, and had a tough first season in New York. It required patience and mental toughness to adapt to a new team, demanding fans and the expectations that came with his long-term contract.But he’s changed his mind since then as his family has grown. Lindor said in an April 2025 interview with USA Today Sports that his kids and wife have become the focus of his life. He also said that failures in personal life on the baseball field just aren't as important as they used to be.Francisco Lindor extends his influence beyond MLBLindor's family priorities are also evident in his charitable endeavors. His wife has been involved in several of the couple’s community initiatives, especially those involving education, youth development, and opportunity for children.In October 2026, Lindor was recognized for their dedication when they were named the recipient of Major League Baseball’s Roberto Clemente Award. The honor is reserved for players who show great character, civic engagement, and philanthropy in addition to their baseball careers.Lindor was honored for his work in education, youth leadership, disaster relief in Puerto Rico, and for young people in Queens, MLB said in its official announcement. His initiatives include supporting Montverde Academy, creating the Francisco Lindor Scholarship Fund and launching Lindor’s Leaders, a development program focused on communication, teamwork, mental health, and leadership.Katia has also been involved in the family’s philanthropy, helping to develop outreach programs and working with community organizations. The recognition, therefore, highlighted the significance of their shared promise to make a difference beyond professional sports.He’s taken steps to make sure his success on the field doesn’t come at the expense of his personal life, from establishing recovery facilities at home to making time for his kids during the MLB season. He and Katia continue to promote a family atmosphere of partnership, discipline, and involvement, while he pursues his goals as one of the New York Mets’ top players.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Scott Boras says 'there's a strong likelihood' Tarik Skubal signs before current CBA expires on Dec. 1
articles.summary: Skubal is the most prized free agent this offseason and could very well ink a record-breaking deal.
articles.body:
All signs point toward an imminent MLB lockout , which would put an immediate stop to the offseason, including the current free-agency cycle. The existing collective bargaining agreement between MLB and the MLB Players Association is set to expire at 11:59 p.m. ET on Dec. 1.

It sounds like the most coveted free agent will have a new deal by then.

Tarik Skubal's agent, Scott Boras, told MLB Network Radio that "there's a strong likelihood" the left-handed pitcher picks his team in the next nine days.

"I think it's pretty clear that we're certainly going to more than likely make a decision before Dec. 1," Boras said. "We have enough information, we have enough involved, we're deep into these negotiations. There's a strong likelihood. "Could it be that it doesn't happen? That could happen. But I'd say there's a strong likelihood that this moves forward because it frankly impacts maybe 10-to-15 pitching decisions by other teams that are related to this decision."

"I think it's pretty clear that we're certainly going to more than likely make a decision before Dec. 1," Boras said. "We have enough information, we have enough involved, we're deep into these negotiations. There's a strong likelihood.

"Could it be that it doesn't happen? That could happen. But I'd say there's a strong likelihood that this moves forward because it frankly impacts maybe 10-to-15 pitching decisions by other teams that are related to this decision."

The New York Mets have been considered the frontrunner to land Skubal , a two-time Cy Young Award winner who finished this past season with the Los Angeles Dodgers after they acquired him in a seismic trade with the Detroit Tigers ahead of the deadline .

The Dodgers are reportedly in the mix to secure the southpaw's long-term services, too, as are the Toronto Blue Jays and San Diego Padres.

New York, according to former Mets GM and current MLB Network Radio analyst Jim Duquette, extended the 30-year-old Skubal an initial offer for nine years and nearly $400 million .

That offer would result in the highest average annual value (AAV) for a free-agent starting pitcher ever. At the moment, the AAV record in that department is held by Max Scherzer and Justin Verlander, both of whom the Mets previously inked to deals worth $43.3 million in AAV.

articles.title: Luis Gil, Tigers Agree to Contract After Yankees Exit, MLB Rumors on Details for 2024 AL ROY's Deal
articles.summary: Former New York Yankees right-handed starting pitcher and 2024 American League Rookie of the Year Luis Gil agreed to a one-year, $2.3 million contract with the Detroit Tigers, according to Jeff Passan of ESPN.
articles.body:
Former New York Yankees right-handed starting pitcher and 2024 American League Rookie of the Year Luis Gil agreed to a one-year, $2.3 million contract with the Detroit Tigers, according to Jeff Passan of ESPN.

Gil pitched in five seasons (2021-2022, 2024-2026) for the Yankees. In 56 games (51 starts), Gil went 21-11 with a 3.61 ERA (1.29 WHIP) and 272 strikeouts in 269.1 innings (9.1 K/9 rate).

His best season was 2024, when he went 15-7 with a 3.50 ERA (1.19 WHIP) while striking out 171 batters in 151.2 innings.

Gil debuted in the bigs in 2021, made six starts and showed promise for the future, posting a 3.07 ERA and striking out 38 batters in 29.1 innings.

He began the 2022 season in Triple-A with the Scranton/Wilkes-Barre RailRiders and made one spot start with the Yankees. Unfortunately, Gil struggled on both levels and ultimately underwent Tommy John surgery in May 2022.

Gil was out for the rest of 2022 and all of 2023 minus a pair of starts for Single A-Tampa in the latter season. However, he thrived in 2024, helping the Yankees win their first pennant in 15 years along the way. Gil won all six of his May starts, including a 14-strikeout effort against the Chicago White Sox on May 18.

Unfortunately, Gil didn't get the opportunity to build off his 2024 season momentum. He suffered a high-grade lat strain in March 2025 and didn't make his debut until August. Gil posted a good ERA (3.32) over 11 starts but notably saw his strikeout numbers dip (41 in 57.0 innings) and WHIP rise (1.40).

Gil struggled in 2026. In nine games (four starts), Gil went 1-2 with a 4.61 ERA (1.43 WHIP) with 17 strikeouts in 27.1 innings. He was optioned to Triple-A Scranton/Wilkes Barre on April 26. Unfortunately, Gil dealt with right shoulder inflammation and missed three months last season. The Yankees non-tendered him in November, making Gil a free agent.

Now Gil will get a fresh start now in his second MLB home. Hopefully Gil can finally enjoy a multi-year string of good health, which has unfortunately evaded him in his MLB tenure.

articles.title: Tarik Skubal, Mets Agree to Historic $450M Contract After Dodgers Stint, MLB Rumors Reveal Details
articles.summary: Tarik Skubal just became a very rich man.
articles.body:
Tarik Skubal just became a very rich man.

The New York Mets have reportedly signed him to a nine-year, $450 million contract, per multiple reports, after the Los Angeles Dodgers traded for him last season.

The Dodgers originally acquired Skubal from the Detroit Tigers ahead of the 2026 trade deadline in exchange for three prospects.

Skubal was playing at the time on an expiring $32 million contract that had him set to hit unrestricted free agency ahead of his age-30 season in 2027.

The 29-year-old ace had followed up two AL Cy Young Award campaigns by undergoing a procedure to remove loose bodies from his elbow in May.

Skubal returned in June and bounced back after some early struggles to post a 2.03 ERA through July in his final five starts for the Tigers.

He remained dominant following his move to Los Angeles, marking a 2.61 ERA through 10 regular-season starts with his new club.

Skubal then posted a 2.45 ERA with 14 strikeouts through 11 innings in two postseason starts. He was scheduled for another start in Game 5 of the NLCS, but the Dodgers' flagging offense led to the club being swept by the Milwaukee Brewers instead.

The Mets have shown an appetite for the big splash in the past, which included signing Juan Soto to a 15-year, $765 million deal. Now they'll be hoping Skubal can anchor a rotation that was a major issue for the team in a disappointing 2026 season whenever baseball returns amid a likely lockout.

articles.title: MLB Winners and Losers of Tarik Skubal, New York Mets Agreeing to $450M Contract
articles.summary: The biggest domino of the 2026-27 Major League Baseball offseason has officially fallen, with two-time Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal signing a doubly record-setting nine-year, $450 million deal with the New York Mets.
articles.body:
The biggest domino of the 2026-27 Major League Baseball offseason has officially fallen, with two-time Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal signing a doubly record-setting nine-year, $450 million deal with the New York Mets.

The news was first broken by New York Post's Jon Heyman , with ESPN's Jeff Passan coming through two minutes later with the contract figures.

There was a report on Friday evening that the Mets had already offered Skubal a nine-year, $400M contract earlier in the offseason. And if that was leaked for the sole purpose of driving Steve Cohen and the Mets to increase their offer, mission accomplished.

Starting out with the blatantly obvious biggest winner, who stand out as the winners and losers of this monumental signing?

The team that signed Tarik Skubal is one of the winners of Tarik Skubal's signing?

Well, thank goodness you're here, Captain Obvious. We couldn't have solved that one without you.

Perhaps more than anything, though, mediocre starting pitching is what has doomed this team over the past two seasons.

You would think that for the sheer amount of money they spend on their roster, the Mets would have someone other than Nolan McLean in their starting rotation worth building around.

But while a Yankees-Dodgers World Series rematch would hypothetically feature a Game 4 duel between Carlos Rodón and Tyler Glasnow, the Mets were (prior to signing Skubal) looking at either Christian Scott or Zac Thornton as their Game 2 starter, with possibly both Kodai Senga and Sean Manaea rounding out the rotation.

They simply had to do something drastic, which is why seemingly everyone in the tea-leaf-reading business reached an unspoken agreement a few weeks ago that the Mets were the clear favorite to sign Skubal.

Even talk of the Blue Jays, Padres and "mystery teams" as interested parties felt like red herrings, meant to drive up the price that New York was inevitably going to pay.

Now, let's see if it works out better for them than that time they gave both Max Scherzer and Justin Verlander a $43.3M salary in advance of a fire sale for the ages.

Loser: Future of the Mets, If a Salary Cap Is Coming

Rob Manfred and Major League Baseball keep saying that the owners are united and steadfast in their demand for a salary cap in these CBA negotiations.

But does anyone honestly believe that the Dodgers and the Mets want that to happen? After all the future spending they've already done over the past half-decade?

Maybe the biggest question of this whole ordeal has been: How do they handle these gargantuan contracts, when guys like Shohei Ohtani, Juan Soto, Aaron Judge and now Tarik Skubal are single-handedly due more than 15 percent of the proposed salary cap?

Can't void contracts already signed, and can't imagine other owners are going to be on board with just sort of grandfathering in a few superstar contracts to help out the traditional big spenders.

So, with the addition of Skubal's $50M salary, the 2028 Mets have a tax payroll in which Skubal, Bo Bichette, Francisco Lindor, Marcus Semien and Devin Williams are at a combined sum of $216.1M in 2028. If they have to somehow fit that under a $258.2M ceiling, that leaves them $42.1M to fill out the rest of the roster?

Whatever the future picture looks like, though, Steve Cohen and Co. went into these talks with Skubal, knowing full well that a salary cap was the league's goal, and they still saw fit to squeeze one more blockbuster in under the wire.

It makes them one of the top teams to beat in 2027. But if MLB gets its way this winter, the Mets could be in a really tough spot from there.

Winner: The Next Crop of Elite Free Agent Pitchers

Next winter's class of free agent starting pitchers is looking underwhelming, at least in the "young enough to sign a massive contract" division. Joe Ryan (in advance of his age-32 season) and Logan Gilbert (in advance of his age-31 season) will certainly generate a lot of interest, but nothing compared to Skubal's market.

Similar story the following offseason, where George Kirby, Hunter Brown and Reid Detmers are looking like the biggest draws under the age of 33.

Three years from now, though, is when Paul Skenes will hit the open market for the first time, assuming he doesn't sign a long-term extension before then.

And while Skubal is already 30, Skenes won't turn 28 until two months into the first season of his new contract—quite the byproduct of making his MLB debut 10 months after getting drafted.

Two years after that is when the 2026 Cy Young winners, Cam Schlittler and Jacob Misiorowski are scheduled to hit free agency.

We shall see what happens between now and their respective times to cash in. Skenes already had a much less impressive season in 2026 than he did in 2024-25, and the ongoing CBA negotiations could result in a new cap-driven world in which $40M+ salaries simply don't exist.

But it does feel like one of those three is likely to be the next "got to have him" pitcher up for grabs, and Skubal resetting the bar with this mammoth contract ought to pay dividends for the superstar arm that follows him.

Excluding Shohei Ohtani, the previous largest contract ever signed with a pitcher was Yoshinobu Yamamoto's 12-year, $325M deal with the Los Angeles Dodgers.

Moreover, excluding Ohtani again, the largest AAV on a pitcher's contract was the $43.3M marks that both Justin Verlander and Max Scherzer received from the Mets earlier this decade.

Both of those records now belong to Skubal at $450M and $50M, respectively.

Thanks to inflation, those records are, of course, made to be broken. Yamamoto broke Gerrit Cole's record, who broke Stephen Strasburg's record, who broke David Price's record and so on and so forth. (Remember when Barry Zito getting a seven-year, $126M deal was an historic investment?)

But could you imagine if Yamamoto had signed something like a three-year, $84M deal instead and was also a free agent right now, two years younger than Skubal and only slightly less dominant over the past three seasons?

Could he have signed basically the same contract that Skubal did?

Perhaps even a slightly more lucrative one?

Yamamoto does have the ability to opt out after 2029—which could make for a wild winter with both him and Paul Skenes (and Elly De La Cruz) available—but it feels like he is being woefully underpaid at this point, with an AAV roughly 60 percent of Skubal's.

It was a nice three-year run with the crown of highest-paid pitcher, though. He certainly backed it up with his postseason prowess, especially in 2025.

Winner: Teams with Controllable Starting Pitchers to Trade

Now that the biggest ace is off the board, it's time for the Dodgers, Blue Jays, Padres and others to start more earnestly calling the teams who might be willing to trade them an arm to help fill that void instead.

Seattle already parted with Bryce Miller and Logan Evans and surely won't be unloading Logan Gilbert or George Kirby at this point.

Dreams of getting Joe Ryan away from the Twins also vanished in the instant that they signed Sonny Gray to a two-year deal, announcing their intention to contend in 2027.

There are still plenty of options, though.

Reid Detmers has two years of arbitration eligibility remaining, with the Angels presumably at least willing to listen to offers in their current state.

Drew Rasmussen is owed $20M in 2027, but the Rays could be willing to unload that salary for the right package. In San Diego, in particular, he could be the Opening Day starter for less than half the cost of one year of Skubal.

The Yankees have an excess of starting pitchers and ought to be willing to move at least one of Ryan Weathers, Will Warren or Luis Gil.

Or in the "buy low candidate with multiple years of control left" department, Pittsburgh's Mitch Keller, Atlanta's Spencer Strider and Cincinnati's Andrew Abbott could all be prime targets.

Even though we're talking about teams that theoretically had room in their budget to sign Skubal, trading for 1-3 years of any of those pitchers may well be preferable to going to five years at $20M+ apiece in a bidding war for Trevor Rogers or Freddy Peralta.

On the free agency front, it has been 'Skubal this' and 'Skubal that' since the offseason began.

That's partially because he is such an incredible talent, but perhaps more so because of the lack of other must-have players in this free agency cycle.

When the Mets whiffed on Kyle Tucker last year, they quickly pivoted to Bo Bichette, also making him one of the nine players who received a nine-figure contract. It was the fifth consecutive offseason in which teams invested a combined sum of at least $2.9 billion in free agents.

This winter, though, Skubal plausibly could be the only player who signs for at least $100M.

There are several candidates to join him in that club—namely Randy Arozarena, Seiya Suzuki, Teruaki Sato, Freddy Peralta and Trevor Rogers—but there's no guarantee any of them will get nine figures.

Also, when the Mets pivoted from Tucker to Bichette, that was like settling for a grape snow cone after finding out the concession stand was out of cherry syrup. Conversely—and with all due respect to Rogers and Peralta—pivoting from Skubal to whomever you deem to be the next-best pitcher on the market is like planning on a cherry snow cone and coming away with a small, not even fresh popcorn.

Of course, with the lockout at our doorstep, free agency buzz was about to completely disappear, anyway. But it's just weird that it's not even December and the one big fish in the pond has already been caught.

Shortly after Skubal was dealt to the Dodgers at the trade deadline, Tigers president of baseball operations Scott Harris said they previously tried to get him to sign an extension, only to be informed that Skubal was committed to reaching free agency.

Skubal's agent, Scott Boras, subsequently said that the offer was $75M for four years, and that it came before the first of his back-to-back Cy Young seasons.

Who knows if there were other offers along the way or for precisely what amounts, but the long and short of it is that Skubal (with Boras' guidance) bet on himself, and he has now cashed in to an exponential degree.

Pre-arbitration long-term extensions have become all the rage lately, with guys like Kevin McGonigle, Konnor Griffin and JJ Wetherholt agreeing to eight-year or nine-year deals for north of $100M seemingly an hour after making their MLB debuts.

But Boras typically doesn't let his clients play that game, with the exception of Cooper Pratt this past spring.

It doesn't always pan out—see: Zac Gallen—but Boras strongly encourages his guys to keep their eyes on the pot of gold at the end of the rainbow; to play out their pre-arbitration and arbitration years before really cashing in as soon as they're able to do so.

And now Skubal is one of 45 active players (20 of them represented by Boras ) who is making at least $25M per year on a contract of at least five years.

First of all, the best free agent on the market didn't sign with the Los Angeles Dodgers, even though they were trying to sign him.

Did you know that was allowed to happen in today's era of Major League Baseball?

What, they couldn't figure out a way to pay him and his descendants $700M in $3.5M annual installments for the next two centuries, or something comparably enraging to the vast majority of fans?

But the thing that really makes the Dodgers a loser in this bidding war is that they didn't just fail to sign a star player.

Sure, he was great for those two-plus months in Dodger Blue. He made 10 regular season starts with a 2.61 ERA, as well as two postseason starts with a 2.45 ERA.

[He did take the L in Game 1 of the NLCS, but that was mostly the product of the Dodgers not recording one extra-base hit in that game. Allowing two runs in five innings of work against one of the most potent offenses in the sport is a pretty decent outing.]

They didn't win a ring, though. And considering they were already 10 games up in the NL West when they traded for him, it's not like he was the missing link that got them into the postseason.

Basically, they gave up an upper echelon prospect (Zyhir Hope) and a pair of pitchers (River Ryan and Brady Smith) for nothing. It didn't even give them a leg up in the bidding war.

articles.title: Tarik Skubal Signs with Mets: Latest Updates, MLB Rumors and Contract Details to Blockbuster Deal
articles.summary: The Tarik Skubal sweepstakes are over, and the New York Mets have emerged victorious.
articles.body:
The Tarik Skubal sweepstakes are over, and the New York Mets have emerged victorious.

B/R contributor Jon Heyman was the first to report that the Mets were signing Skubal, who was universally considered to be the top available free agent this offseason. Skubal won back-to-back AL Cy Young Awards with the Tigers in 2024 and 2025, before posting a 2.72 ERA across 26 starts in a season split between Detroit and the Los Angeles Dodgers.

Here's everything we know so far about Skubal's deal to go to Queens.

Legendary Mets radio voice Howie Rose retired at the conclusion of the 2026 season. He, we think, was joking with his response to the Skubal signing:

This is a good point by Mark Zuckerman of Nats Journal:

Even if the next CBA were to ease a salary cap in, it's not as though Skubal or Juan Soto's deals are expiring any time soon. Bo Bichette only has a maximum of two seasons left on his deal, but the Mets did just give an eight-year/$95 million extension to A.J. Ewing.

All 30 owners might be united on a salary cap right now. The question is whether Cohen and some other "big-market" owners will stay that way. If a cap came, not only would they lose an advantage, but it would leave them with very little space to spend the next few offseasons.

According to Mitch Bannon of The Athletic , the Blue Jays offered Skubal a nine-year deal worth "a little over $400 million."

That's a very nice offer, but it's not particularly close to the $450 million that the Mets ultimately gave Skubal, even if that deal does include some deferrals. It's unclear if another team made a closer offer to New York's than Toronto did.

If you're wondering approximately how much Skubal will make per start in his new deal, Spotrac founder Michael Ginnitti provided this estimate:

With Skubal off the board, could a bunch of free agents now be about to sign?

Perhaps the next name to watch could be Teruaki Sato. While many free agents would probably like to sign before the lockout, Sato needs to or he will have to go back to Japan for the 2026 season. A report from Yahoo! Japan Sunday indicated that both the Mets and Phillies could be at the forefront of the sweepstakes for the reigning Nippon Professional Baseball MVP.

Dodgers didn't make offer to retain Skubal

According to ESPN's Alden González, the Dodgers didn't wind up making an offer to try to retain Skubal after acquiring him before this past summer's trade deadline:

This will also invite speculation about whether Dodgers owner Mark Walter's legal troubles have led to some purse-tightening this offseason.

Some striking similarities to Max Scherzer

Skubal is signing with the Mets before his age-30 season, as opposed to Scherzer joining New York when he was 37. So this isn't an exact comparison, but it's still worth noting.

Scherzer became a star with the Tigers, winning his first Cy Young Award in 2013 while pitching for Detroit. In the final season of a seven-year contract, the Washington Nationals traded Scherzer—along with Trea Turner—to the Dodgers in 2021. He spent just half a season with the Dodgers before heading to the Mets in free agency on a three-year, $130 million deal.

Skubal won his first two Cy Young Awards with the Tigers. In his contract year, he was traded to the Dodgers. Skubal went 5-2 with a 2.61 ERA in 10 starts with the Dodgers, but like Scherzer, didn't reach the World Series with Los Angeles. Also like Scherzer, Skubal went to free agency and left the Dodgers for a record-setting deal with the Mets.

B/R correctly predicted on Nov. 4 that Skubal would both sign with the Mets and get nine years.

However, the $450 million Skubal received is well above the $387 million total we predicted (which still would have been a record-setting total.) It will be interesting to hear if any other teams sniffed the total guaranteed money Skubal got from the Mets with their offer.

Additionally, B/R projected that Skubal's deal would include an opt out after 2031, the fifth season of the deal. That did not happen. Of course, Skubal got such a good deal that he doesn't really need any opt out and can lay down roots in Flushing.

Since the start of the 2024 season, Skubal leads all MLB starters with 18.0 WAR, with FanGraphs saying the next closest over that period at Cristopher Sánchez (17.4), Chris Sale (15.9) and Paul Skenes (15.0).

The only real concern about Skubal—who will pitch next season at 30 years old—is how he will hold up.

Skubal did have Tommy John surgery in 2017 as a collegiate pitcher, and then flexor tendon surgery as a member of the Tigers in August of 2022. This past season, he underwent the innovative "NanoScope" procedure to remove loose bodies from his left elbow. That surgery allowed him to return to the mound in less than six weeks.

When healthy, Skubal is arguably the best pitcher in baseball. Steve Cohen, David Stearns and the Mets are betting Skubal will be able to remain healthy not only in 2027, but over the lifetime of the most lucrative deal ever given to a pitcher.

Here are some of the instant reactions to the Mets signing Skubal.

ESPN's Jeff Passan reports that Skubal's deal with the Mets will pay him $450 million over nine seasons.

That deal gives Skubal the largest total guarantee a pitcher has ever received in a contract, blowing former teammate Yoshinobu Yamamoto's $325 million out of the water.

Additionally, Skubal gets the largest average annual value in MLB history for someone who is purely a pitcher (so, Shohei Ohtani is excluded). The Mets have previously given $43.3 million average annual values to both Justin Verlander and Max Scherzer. Former Met Zack Wheeler had the highest AAV among active contracts at $42 million with the Philadelphia Phillies.

Per SNY's Chelsea Janes , Skubal's deal does not include any opt-out clauses.

Ken Rosenthal of The Athletic reports that Skubal will be paid a $45 million signing bonus up front. That's a nice clause in general, but particularly since there is labor uncertainty in 2027.

According to Will Sammon of The Athletic , there is a full no-trade clause included in the pact.

Joel Sherman of The New York Post says that of the $450 million, $30 million is deferred.

articles.title: Dodgers' Top Free-Agent, Trade Targets After Tarik Skubal's $450M Mets Contract
articles.summary: Tarik Skubal's time with the Los Angeles Dodgers was short-lived as the star ace signed with the New York Mets on Sunday.
articles.body:
Tarik Skubal's time with the Los Angeles Dodgers was short-lived as the star ace signed with the New York Mets on Sunday.

Skubal, who was traded to Los Angeles from the Detroit Tigers in August, signed a nine-year, $450 million contract with the Mets, per ESPN's Jeff Passan , marking the largest contract for a pitcher in MLB history.

Now, the Dodgers are looking for someone to replace Skubal, if that's possible. Here are some potential candidates.

The top free agent pitcher is off the market, but the second-best option is still available.

Trevor Rogers can't quite compare to Skubal, but he's a year younger and has posted respectable numbers over the last few years. He recorded a 4.03 ERA, 157 strikeouts and a 1.18 WHIP with the Baltimore Orioles last season.

Los Angeles could pick him up for a much more affordable price than it would have had to pay for Skubal, giving it flexibility to use elsewhere.

With Skubal now having signed elsewhere, the Dodgers could pivot to retaining a different free agent: Eric Lauer.

The Dodgers didn't get to experience much of Lauer after trading for him in May, as he played just 14 games before his season-ending left elbow injury. He was solid when he was healthy, though, recording a 7-2 record with a 4.50 ERA, a 1.22 WHIP and 46 strikeouts.

He'd certainly be a buy-low option, but at 31, he could still have some of his best days ahead of him.

With a starting rotation that already features plenty of talent, the Dodgers' best course of action could instead be to target a bullpen option.

Adrian Morejon is one of the best free-agent relievers this offseason. The former San Diego Padre recorded a 2.83 ERA and a 1.08 WHIP with 107 strikeouts across 76 appearances and 86.0 innings. He also had a 9-3 record.

The Dodgers came up short in the postseason in part because of their bullpen, and Morejon could be the missing piece for the 2024 and 2025 champs.

articles.body: Tarik Skubal, the two-time Cy Young Award winner who was the top free agent on this offseason’s market, has agreed to record $450 million, nine-year contract with the New York Mets, a person familiar with the negotiations told The Associated Press on Sunday. ESPN has also confirmed the deal. The person spoke on condition of anonymity because the agreement was subject to a successful physical. Skubal’s deal, averaging $50 million annually, is the largest for a pitcher, topping Yoshinobu Yamamoto’s $325 million, 12-year contract with the Los Angeles Dodgers that started in 2024. The previous high for a pitcher’s average salary was $37 million for Jacob deGrom in a $185 million, five-year contract with Texas that began in 2023. It’s the fourth largest deal among all baseball players, trailing Juan Soto’s $765 million, Shohei Ohtani’s $700 million and Vladimir Guerrero Jr.’s $500 million. Skubal’s agreement includes a full no-trade clause and a $45 million signing bonus that is shielded from the management lockout that threatens the 2027 season, the person said. A two-time All-Star left-hander who turned 30 on Nov. 20, Skubal is 43-17 with a 2.42 ERA in 88 starts over the last four seasons, striking out 655 and walking 95 in 546 innings. Skubal had a $32 million salary this year after winning a record amount in salary arbitration. He joins a Mets team that finished last in the NL East at 74-88 despite having baseball’s highest payroll on opening day at roughly $352 million. New York’s starters had a 4.47 ERA, ranking 23rd in the majors. Skubal will top a rotation featuring youngsters Nolan McLean and Christian Scott, with veterans Sean Manaea and Kodai Senga also under contract. Skubal was 12-7 with a 2.72 ERA in 26 starts this year for Detroit and the Los Angeles Dodgers, who acquired him on Aug. 2 for three prospects: right-handers River Ryan and Brady Smith, and outfielder Zyhir Hope. Skubal didn’t pitch for the Tigers between April 29 and June 13 because of surgery to remove a loose body in his pitching elbow. Dodgers head team physician Dr. Neal ElAttrache used a NanoNeedle scope 2.0 to perform the procedure, designed to speed recovery. Skubal was 1-1 with a 2.45 ERA in a pair of postseason starts for the Dodgers. He beat Atlanta in a Division Series opener and lost Game 1 of the NL Championship Series against Milwaukee, allowing two runs over five innings in a 2-1 defeat. The Brewers went on to sweep the two-time defending World Series champions. He averaged 96.8 mph with his four-seam fastball this year, down from 97.6 mph in 2025, when he won his second straight AL Cy Young Award. He threw 38% four-seamers this year, 25.6% changeups, 17.5% sinkers, 13.9% sliders and 5% curveballs. Skubal is 66-44 with a 3.02 ERA in 160 starts and three relief appearances over seven major league seasons with 1,075 strikeouts over 925 1/3 innings.

articles.title: Tarik Skubal reportedly joins Mets on record-breaking, 9-year, $450 million contract
articles.summary: The top MLB free agent is heading to New York on the largest contract ever given to a pitcher.
articles.body:
Tarik Skubal has found his new landing spot: After half a season with the Los Angeles Dodgers, the two-time Cy Young Award winner has agreed to sign with the New York Mets on a nine-year, $450 million deal, per multiple media reports.

The contract breaks the record for the largest deal for a pitcher in MLB history, with Skubal set to earn $50 million in average annual value. The previous record was set in 2023 when the Dodgers signed Yoshinobu Yamamoto to a 12-year, $325 million deal; Skubal's new contract eclipses that amount by $125 million.

Skubal, who turned 30 on Friday, will reportedly receive a $45 million signing bonus as part of the deal, which also includes a no-trade clause. The bonus will be paid to Skubal immediately upon signing , essentially giving him a full season of pay ahead of the projected Dec. 1 lockout , USA Today's Bob Nightengale reported.

The Mets had emerged as the front-runners to sign the ace, with the team's initial offer reportedly a nine-year deal worth nearly $400 million . Skubal and his agent, Scott Boras, appear to have bumped that up significantly in negotiations.

Despite having the most expensive payroll in baseball this past season, the Mets finished the 2026 season last in the NL East with a 74-88 record. New York will hope the addition of an ace in Skubal will help change their fortunes for next season.

Shortly before Sunday's signing was reported, Boras had indicated a desire to agree to a contract before Dec. 1 , when the current collective bargaining agreement between the league and the players' association is set to expire and the team owners are expected to lock out the players.

ESPN's Alden González reported that the Dodgers had interest in signing Skubal but did not end up making an offer due to the uncertainty around the new CBA. Los Angeles also has a very expensive payroll and the potential for a salary cap might have complicated how much the Dodgers were willing to pay to bring Skubal back.

With Skubal pitching on the final year of his contract with the Detroit Tigers in 2026, he was sent to the Dodgers in a bombshell trade just ahead of the trade deadline. Skubal joined a stacked L.A. rotation , giving the lefty starter a new challenge after six seasons with the Tigers.

From his Los Angeles debut to an emotional return to Detroit , Skubal pitched well in Dodger blue to finish the 2026 season. He started Game 1 of the NLDS, beginning L.A.'s playoff run by retiring 15 straight batters .

Even so, the addition of Skubal wasn't enough to lead the Dodgers to a three-peat: Skubal's 2-1 loss against the Milwaukee Brewers in the NLCS kicked off a surprising sweep on the way to the Brewers capturing their long-awaited first World Series title .

Now heading to New York, Skubal is firmly in his prime, with his 2026 season only slightly paused by left elbow surgery (and a shortened healing time thanks to an innovative scope procedure ).

Skubal entered this offseason as the top free agent in the sport and one with the kind of expected salary that only a few teams could afford.

The New York Mets committed $450 million and nine years to star ace Tarik Skubal on Sunday as they look to compete for a World Series, but the move wasn't enough to make them favorites to win it all in 2027.

In fact, Skubal's former team is the favorite to win the World Series. Per FanDuel Sportsbook , the Los Angeles Dodgers are the favorites to win at +390, while the New York Mets have the fifth-best odds at +1700.

The Mets have plenty of talent with players like Skubal, Juan Soto, Francisco Lindor and Bo Bichette, though they have $1.6 billion invested in those four players alone, which leaves them with little flexibility to make other moves.

The Dodgers, meanwhile, have stars like Shohei Ohtani, Freddie Freeman and more, but have done a good job of filling in the roster around them as well. Still, Los Angeles had the best odds to win the World Series last year but lost in the NLCS.

The Mets are coming off a 74-88 season that saw them miss the postseason for a second year in a row. Whether signing the top pitcher on the free-agent market can be the difference-maker remains to be seen.

articles.title: “It's something I wanted to give back in return”: How Shohei Ohtani made a 13-year-old heart patient’s dream come true with a heartfelt Dodgers surprise
articles.summary: Shohei Ohtani gave one young Dodgers fan a night he will never forget.
articles.body: Shohei Ohtani gave one young Dodgers fan a night he will never forget. On May 16, 2024, the Japanese superstar surprised 13-year-old Albert Lee before Los Angeles faced the Cincinnati Reds. Albert had undergone three open-heart surgeries since he was three and now lives with only half a heart. What began as a chance to meet his favourite baseball player soon turned into something much bigger.Ohtani handed Albert a signed jersey, invited him to throw the ceremonial first pitch and then revealed another surprise. Albert and his family would watch the game from a suite. The teenager could hardly believe what was happening. “What the heck just happened?” he said after meeting his idol. Shohei Ohtani planned a special surprise for Albert on Dodgers bobblehead nightThe moment came on Ohtani's first bobblehead night as a Dodgers player. With plenty of attention surrounding the giveaway, the Japanese star wanted to make the occasion special for someone who needed it.Before the Dodgers' game against Cincinnati on May 16, Ohtani walked into the team's interview room to meet Albert. Dr. Gary Satou, director of Pediatric Echocardiography at UCLA Mattel Children's Hospital, had recommended the teenager for the experience.Albert was already a huge Dodgers fan and followed Ohtani closely. However, he had no idea that his favourite player was about to walk into the room.Ohtani greeted him with a handshake and asked, “Nervous?” He then gave Albert a signed jersey before revealing the biggest surprise. The 13-year-old would throw the ceremonial first pitch, with Ohtani himself waiting behind the plate to catch it.But the surprises did not end there. Ohtani also told Albert that he and his family would watch the game from a suite. The news left the teenager stunned.For a young fan who had spent years dealing with serious heart problems, the evening offered a welcome break from hospital visits and medical challenges. It also gave his family a memory they could share long after the game ended.Shohei Ohtani explained why he wanted to make the young fan happyOhtani later explained the reason behind his gesture. Speaking through interpreter Will Ireton during the Dodgers' May 16, 2024, event, the two-time American League MVP said he could imagine how much such an experience would mean to a child.“If I was a child [in need] I would be very happy as well,” Ohtani said. “It's something I wanted to [give back] in return.”The comment offered a simple explanation for why he wanted to use his first bobblehead night for something more personal. Rather than keeping the attention on himself, Ohtani helped create a moment that put a young fan at the centre of the evening.Albert's reaction was just as memorable. After Ohtani left the room, the teenager finally found the words to describe the meeting.“What the heck just happened?” he said.He also recalled his first impression of the Dodgers superstar. “First thing I thought was like, ‘Oh, he's tall.’”Albert then admitted, “I couldn't even breathe for like 30 seconds.”In Albert’s case, the evening was about much more than a signed jersey or a ceremonial pitch. He got to meet his favourite player, throw a pitch to him and watch the Dodgers with his family. articles.title: For the Mets, signing Tarik Skubal is a loud reminder of their financial might and an expensive step back toward contention
articles.summary: The Mets have a long to-do list this offseason. They accomplished their No. 1 objective by landing Skubal.
articles.body:
Two years ago, as the baseball industry descended upon Dallas for the annual winter meetings, news broke of a truly jaw-dropping free-agent agreement: The New York Mets had signed outfielder Juan Soto to a 15-year deal worth $765 million, the largest contract in North American professional sports history. It was the result of a generational talent hitting the open market at an unusually young age, a super-agent in Scott Boras fetching an unthinkable sum in free agency and an outrageously wealthy owner in Steve Cohen willing to bid as high as necessary to get the deal done.

That seismic Soto contract set the stage for another lucrative link-up between Boras and Cohen two years later, this time featuring a particularly special pitcher. On Sunday, two-time Cy Young Award winner Tarik Skubal reportedly agreed to a nine-year, $450 million deal with the Mets .

This time, Boras' top client couldn't wait for the winter meetings. With a work stoppage looming in the form of an expected lockout amid contentious CBA negotiations, it became apparent early this offseason that Skubal's free agency would be expedited. While it's not entirely uncommon for premium free agents to sign in November — last offseason, Dylan Cease (another Boras client) agreed to a seven-year deal with Toronto the night before Thanksgiving — it's typical for the best players available to take a bit more time.

But Skubal reportedly met with four teams in person last week: the Mets, Blue Jays, Padres and Dodgers, whom he pitched for down the stretch following a trade from Detroit. And with a de facto deadline approaching on Dec. 1 — and an unknown economic system potentially awaiting on the other side of the lockout — it was clear that Boras and Skubal wanted to finalize a deal this month.

After all, the unusual circumstances shrouding this offseason weren't expected to meaningfully hamper Skubal's appeal as a free agent. There was little doubt that with enough big spenders hungry for upgrades on the mound, the terrific southpaw would surpass the previous record for a free-agent contract for a pitcher, the 12-year, $325 million deal the Dodgers gave to Japanese sensation Yoshinobu Yamamoto in December 2023.

What was unclear, though, was just how much higher Skubal's contract could climb. Precedents tend to matter in such negotiations — it did not feel like an accident that Yamamoto's total barely edged the previous record, set by Gerrit Cole with $324 million over nine years — and that made it difficult to project the degree to which suitors would be willing to go beyond the Yamamoto and Cole totals to secure Skubal.

There was also another benchmark for Boras and Skubal to target: the average annual value record. Cole's mega-deal signed seven years ago landed him an AAV of $36 million, and Yamamoto's was lower due to the length of his contract, so the highest single-season AAV for a pitcher was previously a tie between Max Scherzer and Justin Verlander, the future Hall of Famers who signed shorter-term deals in 2021 and 2022, respectively, that guaranteed them $43.3 million per season. Remember which team they signed with?

This, of course, brings us back to Cohen. It was five years ago that Scherzer — like Skubal, a Boras client who spent the last few months of his contract with the Dodgers following a midseason trade — signed his massive, three-year pact with the Mets, also finalized in the days leading up to a lockout. One year later, Cohen splurged on Verlander, too. The duo pitched together for just a few months before the 2023 Mets disintegrated around them, but those roster moves offered another blaring signal that Cohen is willing to operate like no other owner.

Undeterred by much of anything in the seasons since then — not on-field failures, off-field circuses or a looming labor war centered in part on his unrivaled spending — Cohen has pressed on, flexing his financial advantage whenever possible. And with an urgent need for pitching underscored by another disappointing Mets campaign — the team's third losing season in six years with Cohen as owner — it's no surprise that Skubal emerged as New York's top target to headline its offseason, no matter the cost.

The result is another contract that sent shockwaves through the industry. Skubal joined Cole and Yamamoto as the only pitchers to secure a free-agent deal of nine years or longer (and Skubal is a year older than Cole was at the time). Now set to make a cool $50 million per season on average, he also obliterated the AAV record for a pitcher. Of course, that makes Skubal the second-highest paid player on his new team after Soto.

Across the league, the ramifications of Skubal's record-smashing contract could be significant in the short and long term. His agreement being finalized well before Dec. 1 could open the door for a flurry of activity, as pitching-needy clubs — whether or not they were chasing Skubal — can now pivot to other arms in free agency or trade. Then there's the matter of how Skubal's gigantic contract and the Mets' lavish spending fit into the larger conversation about baseball's economic system, which is about to be the subject of intense negotiations over the next several months. This deal likely doesn't change much on that front, but it is another reminder of the Mets' outsized financial might.

And for the Mets, the signing of Skubal accomplishes their No. 1 offseason objective, but their to-do list is far from complete as they seek to rebound from a dismal, 74-win season. If anything, this deal refocuses the hot stove spotlight on president of baseball operations David Stearns, whose team-building strategies executed alongside Cohen's exorbitant spending have thus far fallen short of expectations. Stearns presumably gave a hearty thumbs-up to the notion of adding Skubal, but moves of this magnitude tend to elevate beyond those leading the front office, so it's difficult to know how much credit to assign Stearns (or any executive) in a situation such as this.

What we can do is ponder the next steps for Stearns, knowing that Skubal alone cannot elevate the Mets to where they want to be, just as Soto's greatness has gone only so far in his first two seasons in Queens. Right-hander Nolan McLean, 25, might be an ascendant ace behind Skubal, but huge questions remain regarding the rest of New York's pitching staff, so there's more work to be done there.

Alongside Soto, a promising outfield has emerged — Carson Benge finished runner-up in the NL Rookie of the Year race, and AJ Ewing showed enough in his debut season to earn a reported $95 million extension — but the long-term infield plans around shortstop Francisco Lindor are uncertain. A Bo Bichette bounce-back is a must after he exercised his $42 million player option, but even that won't solve the unknowns on the depth chart at second base, first base, DH and even catcher. The bevy of bloated contracts inflating the payroll might not stop Cohen from spending further, but they do make for a complicated roster puzzle for new full-time skipper Andy Green to sort out.

All of these are important, if not urgent, concerns that Stearns needs to address. At the same time, the Mets had to start somewhere in their quest to restore their status as serious contenders.

Signing Tarik Skubal marks an exciting — and historically expensive — first step.

articles.title: New MLB Rumors Reveal Blue Jays' Top Free-Agent Target After Tarik Skubal's $450M Mets Contract

After missing out on top free-agent pitcher Tarik Skubal, the Toronto Blue Jays are reportedly turning their sights on another big swing.

Unlike the massive $450 million deal Skubal reportedly signed with the Mets earlier on Sunday, Peralta is expected to sign around the $25 million range per year, which would also give Toronto more room to keep adding.
